REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-WA-2020-0188 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 22 October 2020 and the current registration period extends to 21 October 2023. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Barry Holloway is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2008. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 37 on Plan DP 574922, located at Lot 12 Great Eastern Highway, Cunderdin WA 6407. The total registered area is 62.8 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 8,000 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

The establishment began operating under the trading name 'AgriPrime Exports' from April 2025 for marketing purposes. The registered entity name remains unchanged. DAFF has not been notified of the new trading name.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

An external overhead conveyor linking the new storage annex to the main outloading facility was installed in January 2025. The conveyor traverses the registered premises boundary. No DAFF approval was sought before installation.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

3. Process Flow Diagram
4. Hazard Analysis
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No site-specific hygiene and sanitation program documented for Broome Pearl & Ag Products Pty Ltd. General industry practices are referenced but no cleaning schedules, chemicals, personnel hygiene procedures or records are defined.

Waste Management Procedure (AOW-WMP-001):
• Scalper screenings / trash: collected in sealed bins; transported off-site to approved composting.
• Oilseed dust: cyclone dust collector; dust collected in sealed bags; removed weekly.
• Linseed meal (pressing by-product): sold to livestock feed market; removed within 48 hours of pressing.
• Chemical waste: fumigant and pesticide containers disposed per APVMA label; manifest maintained.
• Wastewater from cleaning: directed to grease trap; collected by liquid waste contractor monthly.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

Pest Control Program (AOW-PCP-001):
• Rodents: 16 perimeter bait stations (Bromadiolone); monthly inspection; licensed contractor annual review.
• Insects: pitfall traps in each silo; grain temperature probe weekly in storage season; phosphine fumigation when insects detected.
• Bird exclusion: all structural openings sealed; netting at loading conveyor ends.
• Records: Pest Control Log (AOW-PC-01) monthly.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (AOW-TRACE-001):
• Each silo assigned unique ID (silo number + commodity + IP/non-GM status + season).
• Receival dockets link grower → farm block → variety → quantity → silo.
• Dispatch: bill of lading links silo ID → vessel/tanker → destination.
• GM testing records linked to lot reference; retained 5 years (EU requirement).
• One-step-forward / one-step-back trace exercise performed semi-annually.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

Failed Goods Procedure (AOW-FGP-001):
• GM contamination above threshold: lot re-classified as non-Identity Preserved; customer notified; DAFF notified.
• Mycotoxin exceedance: silo placed on HOLD; re-test from secondary sample; if confirmed, dispose to non-food use.
• Pesticide MRL: reject export consignment; segregate; grower liability documented; option to process to domestic oil (if MRL met under FSANZ).
• All non-conformances recorded in AOW-NCR register with root cause analysis.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (AOW-PSP-001):
• Export-cleared grain stored in dedicated silos; not accessible to uncleared grain.
• Identity Preserved (non-GM) lots in dedicated, clearly labelled IP silos.
• Loading procedure: transport unit inspected before loading; last cargo record reviewed; sealed containers sealed at point of loading.
• DAFF sampling completed before loading of each export lot.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.
12. Approval and Review

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Wheatbelt Storage Co is a registered export establishment located at Lot 12 Great Eastern Highway, Cunderdin WA 6407, WA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-WA-2020-0188 and is registered to handle and export Barley under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Barley.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 520 lux packing hall, 400 lux cool store entry, 380 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

The Barley storage utilises an open-front bay design. The bay entrance (6 m wide × 4 m high) is fitted with a chain-link gate for security but provides no insect or bird exclusion. A mesh curtain was installed in 2021 but has sustained damage and does not provide a complete seal. Enclosed processing areas have full pest exclusion measures.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-199, version 2.4, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 4 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: January 2025).

2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Wheatbelt Storage Co used in pulse cleaning, storage and packing operations for export Red Lentils. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Red Lentils during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Hopper

After each intake run: Lock out receiving conveyor. Use compressed air lance to dislodge pulse residue from hopper walls, conveyor trough, and all transition points. Vacuum accumulated screenings and fine material. Inspect underside of conveyor belt for product trapping. Record in Intake Checklist.
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter

After each cleaning run: Remove accumulated screenings from collection trays and hoppers. Brush aspirator screens with dedicated brush to remove lodged seeds. For colour sorter: follow manufacturer's lens cleaning protocol. Vacuum sensor housings. Inspect all filters and replace if blocked. Record in Plant Operator Run Log.
Storage Silos / Bins

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Storage Silos / Bins in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Packing Line / Bagging Machine

End of each shift: Clear all pulse product from the line. Vacuum or brush conveyor belts, weigh hoppers, and bag former guides to remove pulse fines. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe external surfaces of bagging machine and packing bench. Check sealing jaws and heat elements for residue. Record in Shift Log.
Palletising Area / Loading Dock

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Palletising Area / Loading Dock in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Dead-stock accumulation occurs in aspirator collection trays, conveyor trough joints, and under the bagging machine floor plate. These areas are vacuumed or blown out at each run change to prevent insect harbourage.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System
The establishment manager maintains informal notes of cleaning activities as required. There is no standardised form or digital system for recording cleaning events.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES

ATP (adenosine triphosphate) swab testing is used monthly on critical food-contact surfaces to verify cleaning efficacy. Results are recorded in the Surface Hygiene Register alongside the cleaning log.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Wheatbelt Storage Co (conducted 3 April 2025) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.
